title: The screen between Atzilus and Beriya (no recording)
overview: The series has no recording of this chapter. The catalog goes from class 229, which ends inside chapter 50, to class 230, which opens with chapter 52 and says chapter 51 was "basically covered"; the tape that taught it is not in the catalog. What follows only says what the chapter's lines take up, so a reader can find them, and teaches nothing in Rabbi Markel's name. The chapter asks about the *masach* (the screen) between *Atzilus* (the world of Emanation) and *Beriya* (the world of Creation), which the *Malchus* (kingship) of *Atzilus* breaks through. It compares the light seen through the screen to the impression a seal leaves in wax, and roots the screen in the *levush hachashmal* (the garment of *chashmal*), likened to a heap of stones: letters not set in order. It contrasts this screen with the first *tzimtzum* (contraction), the *makom panui* (the empty place), and says the screen divides only for the receivers. It ties this to *yichuda tata'a* (the lower unity) and *yichuda ila'a* (the higher unity), and ends with the Names *MaH* and *BaN* and the *milui* (the spelling out of a letter's name).

sections.title: The light seen through the screen: a seal in wax (not on tape)
sections.summary: The chapter asks about the *masach* between *Atzilus* and *Beriya*, which *Malchus* breaks through: "in Your light we see light" is a light born of the screen, a glow of a glow, like the impression a seal leaves in wax, and it becomes the crown of *Beriya*. The series has no recording of these lines.

sections.title: The root of the screen: a heap of stones, letters out of order (not on tape)
sections.summary: The screen is made from the *levush hachashmal* of the outside of bina; the text likens it to a heap of stones, letters not set in order, which divide, as unordered speech carries no meaning while a *mashal* (analogy) and a riddle hide a meaning that can still be found. The series has no recording of these lines.

sections.title: A full screen, unlike the first tzimtzum, yet a barrier only for the receivers (not on tape)
sections.summary: Because *Atzilus* and *Beriya* have no relation, a screen is needed; the first *tzimtzum*, the *makom panui*, was only a concealment within the Essence, while from *Atzilus* to *Beriya* there is a complete break, made by the One who contracts, so that it divides only for the receivers. The series has no recording of these lines.

sections.title: Baruch shem: the lower unity of Malchus in Beriya (not on tape)
sections.summary: The text calls this the root of *yichuda tata'a*, the glow of the ten sefiros of *Malchus* of *Atzilus* in *Beriya*, and reads the tribes' answer to Jacob as *yichuda ila'a* in *Atzilus* and the lower unity in *Beriya*. The series has no recording of these lines.

sections.title: MaH and BaN, and the milui as the particular from the general (not on tape)
sections.summary: The two unities are also called the Names *MaH* and *BaN*, and the text explains the *milui* of a letter as an explanation of the letter, each spelling out a further particular, like a mashal within a mashal; there is also a *milui* the other way, a concealment within concealment, which is the garment of the screen. The series has no recording of these lines.

notes.text: No class of the series reads this chapter: every line is NOT READ. Class 229 (Tape55-Side2, chapter 50) ends inside chapter 50 at line 21 of that chapter, and class 230 (Tape57-Side1, chapter 52) opens: "chapter 51, we basically we covered it ... There's no special questions" (230 w3-35). So the chapter was taught on a tape that is not in the catalog (probably Tape 56). The file has no lectures, no phrases and no blocks.

The title, overview and section titles and summaries paraphrase the chapter text, not a class, as chapter 49 does for its unrecorded lines; they say what the lines take up and teach nothing in Rabbi Markel's name. The section cuts and passage groupings are by the sense of the text.

The terms' glosses are taken from translit.json and from chapters 9, 44 and 49 of this series (masach, levush hachashmal), not from a class on this chapter. reviewQuestions is left empty: STYLE.md asks for questions answerable from the file, and with no class and no phrases the file has nothing to answer them from.

Class 230's opening (w3-35) is the only thing in the catalog about chapter 51; it says nothing of its content, so it is left to chapter 52's file (as logistics) and not cited here. If the missing tape turns up, this file should be rewritten from it.
